claims.explanation: E01 in logic/experiments.md requires OxfordPets per-image confidence under Full/Medium/Narrow masks and per-sample final-minus-initial training loss. The supplied evidence index and Tables 1–2 contain dataset-aggregated test accuracies, not those individual confidence or loss observations; these aggregates cannot establish differing optimal masks or the positive loss-change tail. No narrower aggregate-accuracy claim substitutes for C01.

E02 specifies a logical hypothesis-class inclusion argument for Fshr and Fsp within Fsmm and Theorem 4.2's distribution-level approximation-error ordering. Installed reported relations compare numeric measurements; neither they nor the experiment families certify universal set containment or strict containment. Table 4's parameter sizes would not discharge this mathematical assertion. The title's strict wording is not silently replaced by a finite empirical accuracy comparison.

Table 1 provides three-seed mean±std test accuracy under ILM, 200 epochs, and the fixed ResNet-18/50 training conditions of E03. One best-baseline aggregation includes PAD, NARROW, MEDIUM and FULL; its ResNet-18 scope is exactly the ten datasets named by excluding DTD, while ResNet-50 includes all eleven. Both scopes also require the reported AVERAGE row to exceed every baseline. DTD is treated as the stated ResNet-18 exception, not as an additional positive comparison. Reported spreads and precision remain in source measurements; no significance test is invented.

Table 2 gives the ViT-B32 mean accuracies for all eleven datasets and the AVERAGE row under E04's default LR=0.001 (not the separate tuned UCF101 result). C04 additionally asserts additive gains of 21.8, 15.4 and 7.3 percentage points over the best baselines on Flowers102, Food101 and SUN397. The catalog's reported comparisons support ordering and multiplicative ratios, not these asserted additive differences or exact aggregate levels 72.4% versus 65.2%. A majority/average ordering alone would omit substantive numeric conditions.

Table 3 reports ResNet-18, ILM, three-seed mean±std accuracy for the four actual ablations. E05 identifies feature-rich CIFAR10/Flowers102/UCF101 and large-data CIFAR10/SVHN/GTSRB/SUN397, giving the two component-removal scopes. A third conjunct preserves the explicitly highlighted GTSRB/Flowers102 three-channel advantage; a best-baseline conjunct requires the full SMM AVERAGE over all eleven datasets to beat all three ablations, including single-channel. These method-dependent scopes require a conjunction rather than one uniform all-baseline comparison; especially is not converted into an invented numerical margin.

Table 5 has ResNet-18/50 numeric pixel accesses and batch times (batch 256, A100) plus the categorical REQUIRE BACKPROPAGATION=NO cell for patch-wise interpolation. The full statement includes that categorical algorithmic condition as well as the explicit counts/times and spreads. Numeric ordering alone cannot assert NO backpropagation or all stated magnitudes; reported catalog relations have no categorical-equality or exact reported-value relation. The separate ViT table is not substituted for the named ResNet condition.
